           MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER AND SECOND REPLY OF
                   NORTHERNGRID ENROLLED PARTIES

       Pursuant to Rules 212 and 213 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure,1 Avista Corporation; PacifiCorp;

NorthWestern Corporation; Portland General Electric Company; Puget Sound Energy, Inc.;

Idaho Power Company; Nevada Power Company and Sierra Pacific Power Company; and

MATL LLP (collectively, the “Enrolled Parties”) respectfully move for leave to answer and

submit this limited second reply to the October 1, 2026 Motion for Leave to Answer and Answer

filed by the CREPC 1920 Ad Hoc Committee on behalf of the NorthernGrid Relevant State

Entities (“RSE Answer”).2

       The Enrolled Parties request waiver of Rule 213(a)(2) to the extent necessary. Good

cause exists because this filing is confined to correcting the RSE Answer’s descriptions of the

Enrolled Parties’ filed Attachment Ks and August 28, 2026 Motion for Leave to Answer and

 Answer (“Enrolled Parties’ Answer”). The Commission has accepted otherwise-prohibited

answers when they clarify the record and assist its decision-making.3

        The Enrolled Parties appreciate the Relevant State Entities’ substantial engagement

throughout the Order No. 1920 process and do not seek to repeat arguments already presented.4

This second reply identifies three limited record corrections: (1) the filed Attachment Ks provide

voluntary funding mechanisms; (2) the RSE Answer mischaracterizes the Enrolled Parties’

concerns regarding solution-based distribution factor (“DFAX”) analysis; and (3) the filed

Attachment Ks permit portfolio planning.

    I. ANSWER

        A. The Filed Attachment Ks Provide for Voluntary Funding

        The RSE Answer states that benefits to non-jurisdictional utilities “are to be ignored”

under the Enrolled Parties’ method and contrasts that treatment with the RSE Proposal’s

subscription process.5 The filed Attachment Ks, however, provide voluntary funding

mechanisms. Section 3.4.5 (Voluntary Funding Option and Processes for Relevant State Entities

and Interconnection Customers) permits Relevant State Entities and Interconnection Customers

to fund all or part of a Long-Term Regional Transmission Facility or portfolio that otherwise

would not satisfy the selection criteria and Section 3.6.4.2(b) (Hybrid Allocation) permits a non-

beneficiary to accept a specified cost allocation in writing. Those voluntary amounts are

 deducted before remaining costs are allocated to Long-Term Enrolled Party Beneficiaries.6 A

non-jurisdictional entity also may elect to become an Enrolled Party and thereby become eligible

for cost allocation.7 Thus, both proposals provide paths for voluntary participation and funding.

To the extent the RSE Answer suggests that the filed Attachment Ks provide no comparable

voluntary path, it does not accurately describe the filed tariff language.

       B. The RSE Answer Mischaracterizes the Enrolled Parties’ Concerns
          Regarding DFAX
       The RSE Answer responds to the Enrolled Parties’ Answer as though the Enrolled Parties

sole point was that litigation involving PJM renders DFAX unjust and unreasonable.8 The

Enrolled Parties made no such argument. The Enrolled Parties did not ask the Commission to

reject solution-based DFAX categorically or to revisit its acceptance of DFAX in another region;

rather, PJM’s experience was cited to support the narrower proposition that implementation

details matter. The Enrolled Parties’ prior Answer referenced disputes concerning beneficiary

identification, changes in allocation outcomes, and concentrated large-load growth to illustrate

the importance of specifying the proposed methodology in advance.9

       Order No. 1920 requires transmission providers to include in their tariffs an ex ante

Long-Term Regional Transmission Cost Allocation Method.10 The Enrolled Parties’ Answer

explained that the RSE Proposal does not identify the transmission zones or specify how its

proposed solution-based DFAX allocation would be implemented.11 The RSE Answer confirms

 those facts. It states that DFAX implementation details may be included in a future business

practice manual, acknowledges that the Enrolled Parties would later designate the relevant

transmission zones, and offers to provide additional details if the Commission requires more

information.12

        The RSE Answer acknowledges that PJM includes a number of DFAX details in its

tariff.13 This acknowledgement confirms that such implementation provisions can, and should, be

specified in advance of implementation in the form of tariff provisions. A business practice

manual may implement tariff provisions, but it should not provide the determinative elements of

a cost allocation method after Commission acceptance of the tariff. These elements therefore

distinguish the RSE Proposal from the filed Attachment Ks, which state a complete tariffed ex

ante allocation method.14

        Because the RSEs “do not contest that the Enrolled Parties’ ex ante cost allocation

methodology qualifies as just and reasonable,”15 the Commission can accept the Enrolled Parties'

filed methodology without requiring continued development of a different cost allocation method

in a further compliance process.

        C. The Filed Attachment Ks Expressly Permit Portfolio Planning

        The RSE Answer states that the Enrolled Parties “did not, in their compliance filings,

propose they would engage in portfolio planning.”16 The filed Attachment Ks expressly permit

           The RSE Answer also describes the Enrolled Parties’ method as apportioning “the benefits
FERC identified in Order No. 1000.” RSE Answer at 12. The filed Attachment Ks instead allocate costs
using the seven Required Benefits identified in Order No. 1920. See Attachment K § 3.4.3. The relevant
distinction is therefore not whether the proposals use the seven Required Benefits but that the RSE
Proposal also would allocate 10 or 25 percent of post-subscription costs through its proposed DFAX
component.
        15
           Comments of the CREPC 1920 Ad Hoc Committee on Behalf of the NorthernGrid Relevant
State Entities, Docket Nos. ER26-2793-000 et al., at 11 (filed Aug. 5, 2026) (“RSE Comments”).

                                                       4
 portfolio planning. They authorize the Enrolled Parties Planning Committee to use facility-by-

facility or portfolio approaches, provide for selection of portfolios of Long-Term Regional

Transmission Facilities, and apply the cost allocation methodology to a selected facility or

portfolio.17 The filed Attachment Ks also include the incorporation of the State Agreement

Process developed by the RSEs, which allows for evaluation of portfolios.18

    II. CONCLUSION

        The Enrolled Parties appreciate the RSEs’ continued engagement and submit this second

reply solely to correct the foregoing descriptions of the filed Attachment Ks and the Enrolled

Parties’ Answer. The Enrolled Parties respectfully request that the Commission accept this

second reply and consider these clarifications when evaluating the record in these proceedings.
